paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see. The whole road is shouting about the King, and the stones are ready to join in if the people go quiet. Jesus says, "if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out" (Luke 19:40). When Jesus is the King, praise isn't optional decoration, it's the right response, and I'm not about to let a rock out-sing ME.

But look at what happens next. Jesus comes near Jerusalem, sees the city, and weeps over it (Luke 19:41). He says, "If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace!" (Luke 19:42). All that noise on the road, and the city still didn't recognize Him. Jesus gives the reason Himself: "you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God" (Luke 19:44).

So here's the lesson to carry home. Jesus warns that the days will come when Jerusalem's enemies will surround the city and level it to the ground, and He says why: it did not recognize the time of its visitation from God (Luke 19:43-44). That's how serious it is to miss Him, so don't, baker. Keep your eyes open, keep your heart soft, and keep your praise loud, because the King has come, and that's exactly why my ovens stay ready.
